I need help solving my bizzard pc issue

Hey everyone, I need some serious help figuring out a bizarre PC problem that started after a sudden power cut. I’m running a Ryzen 9 5900X on a Gigabyte B550 Gaming X V2 motherboard, and my main RAM kit is a matching pair of 32GB Kingston Fury 3200MHz.

Ever since the power cut, my PC completely refuses to work right with my matching Kingston RAM kit. If I turn XMP on to get my 3200MHz speed, the PC won't even post, or it throws a corrupted fTPM screen saying a new CPU was installed. If I leave XMP off, it boots into Windows, but the second I try to launch a demanding game or a heavy stress test, the whole PC instantly shuts off.

I have done a ton of hardware swapping to isolate the issue, and the results make absolutely no sense:

\-First, I thought it was my power supply acting up under load, so I swapped it out for a completely different PSU, but the exact same crashes kept happening.

\-Next, I took my CPU and Kingston RAM and tested them in a friend's motherboard. With both Kingston sticks plugged into his board, the PC refused to even turn on. It would only boot if I took one stick out.

\-Then, I tried a completely different CPU in my original Gigabyte motherboard using my Kingston RAM. The crashes under gaming loads still happened, and XMP still wouldn't turn on.

Here is the absolute craziest part. Just to see what would happen, I took out one of my Kingston sticks and replaced it with a random 8GB stick I had lying around. For some insane reason, this completely mismatched Kingston + 8GB setup boots perfectly, enables XMP Profile 1 at 3200MHz with zero issues, and doesn't crash at all under heavy gaming loads.

I am completely stumped. If my CPU memory controller or motherboard traces were physically fried by the power cut, how is a mismatched 16GB and 8GB setup running flawlessly at full 3200MHz XMP speed? But if it is just a single dead Kingston RAM stick, why did putting a completely different CPU into my motherboard still cause the system to crash under load?

Has anyone ever experienced a power surge causing a weird double failure like this, or is there some bizarre hardware conflict I am overlooking? Any advice would be amazing.
